chapter: Learning drums and Roy Eldridge's band
title: George Hornsby's orchestra: learning to read
summary: Pianist-bandleader George Hornsby hired him for a 14-piece band; he could read thanks to his mother's teaching.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: So a bandleader from -- where was he from? From the North Side, a wonderful pianist. He was really --

George Hornsby. So he had an orchestra and he said -- he came in the club one night and he said, "Hey, kid, can you read?" I said, "Well, I can make out," you know. So he said, "Well, let me hear something fast." So Gene, who

would always take care of me, you know, he would play something, so he said, "That's pretty good. Here's my address and everything and here's where we rehearse. Now, do you think you could be there tomorrow about 2:00 o'clock?" So I said, "Well, I'll try, you know." So he said, "Well, don't worry about an instrument, because our trumpet player, he's an instrument repair man, so we have all the instruments that we need." So I said okay, and the next day I went, and they had a lot of stock arrangements which were very simple to read, and he said --
Well, could you actually read anything?
The rhythm and time, you know, different quarter notes and eighth rests and all that.
And I began to play with them and he said, "Gee, kid, you're nice." And I stayed with a big band. I guess we were about 14 pieces. And that did it.
And everybody was much older than you.
